Add information derived from Danish CPR numbers

Source: R/add_cpr_info.R
add_cpr_info.Rd

Add selected CPR information without changing the original CPR column.

Usage

add_cpr_info(.data, .cpr_col, ..., .overwrite = FALSE)

Arguments

.data

A data frame or tibble.

.cpr_col

CPR column, unquoted or a literal column-name string.

...

Information to add: bday, byear, sex, koen, valid, status, mod11, age, or age_at() with a reference year or date. Name a selection to choose its output column, e.g. birth_date = bday. With no selections, adds bday, age, sex, mod11, and valid. Bare age uses today's date.

.overwrite

Allow replacing existing output columns? Default FALSE. The CPR source column cannot be replaced.

Value

The input data frame with selected columns added in selection order.

Details

SelectionValue
bdayBirth date, a Date
byearBirth year, an integer
age, age_at()Completed calendar years, an integer
sexInteger, 1 male (odd final digit), 0 female
koenInteger, 1 male, 2 female: the coding of KOEN in the registers of Statistics Denmark
validLogical: ten digits and a real encoded date
statusFactor: why a value is or is not valid
mod11Logical: the modulus-11 checksum

valid checks ten digits and a real encoded calendar date, not whether the number was assigned to a person. Missing and malformed CPRs give valid = FALSE and missing birth date, age, and sex. mod11 is a separate logical checksum, not a requirement for valid. Malformed formats give a missing checksum.

status says what valid cannot: its levels are valid, missing, scientific, wrong_length, non_digit and invalid_date, the problems of diagnose_cpr(), where they are explained. diagnose_cpr() answers for a column, status for each row, so the rows can be filtered or counted by group.

sex and koen hold the same information in two codings. sex is 0/1, which sums and averages directly; koen is 1/2 and compares directly with the KOEN variable of the registers (https://www.dst.dk/da/TilSalg/data-til-forskning/generelt-om-data/dokumentation-af-data/hoejkvalitetsvariable/Folketal/KOEN).

CPR values are cleaned internally with clean_cpr(). To also standardise the source column, use dplyr::mutate(pnr = clean_cpr(pnr)) explicitly. Rows, row order, and input columns are preserved unless .overwrite = TRUE. Duplicate output names are always an error.

CPR parsing, calendar validation, and requested outputs share a single native pass. Multiple age selections reuse the decoded birth date. Pre-cleaning is optional: use clean_cpr() when the source column itself must be standardised for joins or export.

For a single piece of information inside dplyr::mutate() or dplyr::filter(), the vector functions cpr_birth_date(), cpr_age() and friends give the same values. Prefer add_cpr_info() when you need several: it parses each CPR once.

The arguments have a dot prefix, as in dplyr, so that an output name never reaches them: R matches named arguments by partial name before ..., and d = bday or cpr = age_at(year) would otherwise be taken as data or cpr_col.

For 29 February births, age advances on 1 March in non-leap years. A reference before birth gives a negative age. Use an explicit reference for reproducible analysis; today's date changes between runs.

In daos, add_cpr_info() took add, ref_date, year and at arguments, and later the helper age(). Selections and age_at() replace them; each old form gives an error that points to the new one.

See also

age_at(), clean_cpr(), cpr_birth_date()

Examples

df <- data.frame(pnr = c("0101004007", "111111-1118"), year = 2024:2025)
add_cpr_info(df, pnr)
#>           pnr year       bday age sex mod11 valid
#> 1  0101004007 2024 2000-01-01  26   1  TRUE  TRUE
#> 2 111111-1118 2025 1911-11-11 115   0  TRUE  TRUE
add_cpr_info(df, pnr, sex, birth_date = bday)
#>           pnr year sex birth_date
#> 1  0101004007 2024   1 2000-01-01
#> 2 111111-1118 2025   0 1911-11-11
add_cpr_info(df, pnr,
  primoalder = age_at(year), ultimoalder = age_at(year, "ultimo"), sex)
#>           pnr year primoalder ultimoalder sex
#> 1  0101004007 2024         23          24   1
#> 2 111111-1118 2025        113         114   0
add_cpr_info(df, pnr, alder = age_at("2025-07-01"))
#>           pnr year alder
#> 1  0101004007 2024    25
#> 2 111111-1118 2025   113

# Why a value is not valid, and sex as in the registers
bad <- data.frame(pnr = c("0101004007", "3102004007", "1.01004E+08", NA))
add_cpr_info(bad, pnr, status, koen)
#>           pnr       status koen
#> 1  0101004007        valid    1
#> 2  3102004007 invalid_date   NA
#> 3 1.01004E+08   scientific   NA
#> 4        <NA>      missing   NA
